newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian unit trust scheme listed on bourse.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian unit trust scheme listed on bourse.

text.p: A unit trust scheme aiming to attract foreign investors to the Nigerian stock market was listed on the bourse on Monday.
Investment Bank and Trust Company Ltd., a leading player in investment banking, floated the IBTC Nigerian Equity Fund late last year to raise two billion naira from foreign and local investors.
Investors were invited to buy two million units of the scheme at one thousand naira each.
The promoters said 1,505,360 units were taken up by the close of application list in January but did not indicate the level of local or foreign investors' interest.
Atedo Peterside, chief executive officer of IBTC, said on Monday 82.3 percent of the fund's assets had already been invested in equities.
He said new subscribers desiring to buy into the scheme would pay 16 percent more than the initial offer price.
The bid price for the week is 1,113.35 naira while offer price is 1,161.63 naira.
These bid and offer prices were calculated after covering all initial expenses associated with launching the fund, he said.

Peterside said: "The price at which units will be sold by the manager are calculated in accordance with a formula prescribed by the Securities and Exchange Commission and reflect the underlying values of the investments in the funds."
